insights: Separate pass-execution, skipped-pass, analysis-computation and analysis-invalidation events. Timing an analysis computation differs from timing a cache lookup.
Optional-pass veto callbacks all run and combine their answers; required passes bypass veto. Ink proof admission must never be disabled by diagnostic or profitability callbacks.

After-pass invalidation callbacks omit the invalidated IR reference, avoiding observation of dead objects. Read-only references prevent accidental instrumentation mutation; callback ownership lifetime remains an explicit contract.

Instrumentation pseudo-analysis itself never invalidates because it wraps a callback registry, not an IR-dependent semantic result. This is not a precedent for retaining source-dependent proof facts across mutation.

Class-to-pass display mappings populate lazily once, keep the first mapping and return empty for missing entries. Display names and suffix-based special-pass matching are unsuitable as canonical database/proof identities.
